info.title: Tackle Co-Sell for Microsoft Partner Center Customer Engagements
info.description:
This API helps you interact with Microsoft to create and manage co-sell
referrals that you share with Microsoft as well as receive, respond to,
and manage referrals originated by Microsoft.

## Authentication

This API requires a Tackle machine-to-machine (MTM) access token. Issue
your M2M client credentials following the [How to get an M2M client ID
and secret](https://developers.tackle.io/docs/how-to-get-an-m2m-client-id-and-secret)
guide, exchange them for an access token following the [Getting an
access token](https://developers.tackle.io/docs/getting-an-access-token)
guide, then send the token with each request in the `Authorization`
header as `Bearer <access_token>`.

The MTM token supplies the vendor and organization context for the request.
Fine-grained scoped MTM permissions are not enforced for this API yet.

## Related Tackle Co-Sell APIs

Tackle publishes equivalent Co-Sell APIs for other cloud providers. Customer
engagement domain models differ across providers (AWS and Google Cloud
Channel use "opportunities"; Microsoft Partner Center uses "referrals"), so
endpoint paths, request and response shapes, and pagination details are not
interchangeable.

- Tackle Co-Sell for AWS: https://aws.cosell.tackle.io
- Tackle Co-Sell for Google Cloud Channel: https://gcp.cosell.tackle.io

tags.name: Customers
tags.description:
Look up customer accounts in Microsoft Partner Center before
creating a referral. Use these endpoints to determine
`customerProfile.ids` and the `dealSensitivity` value
(`USFed` vs `None`) you should send.

tags.name: Partners
tags.description:
Look up partner organizations in Microsoft Partner Center.
Use the returned `organizationId` when adding a non-Microsoft
partner via `inviteContexts`.

tags.name: Referrals
tags.description: Create, read, update, and list events on Microsoft Partner Center co-sell referrals (both outbound and inbound).

post.summary: Lookup customer info to determine if they are a US federal customer.
post.description:
Looks up the customer in Microsoft Partner Center by company
name and reports whether Microsoft has tagged the account as a
US federal customer. Use this before creating a referral so
you can populate `dealSensitivity` correctly (`USFed` for US
federal customers, `None` otherwise). Returns an empty
`customerInfo` array when no match is found.

200.description: Response containing info if the customer is a US federal customer.

count.description: The number of matching customers in the response.

microsoftCRMId.description: The Microsoft CRM ID of the customer.

dunsId.description: The DUNS ID of the customer.

type.description:
Customer type tag returned by Microsoft. Currently the only
value emitted is `USFed`, indicating the customer is a US
federal customer; the field is omitted otherwise. Treat as a
free-form string and check for the literal `USFed` rather than
parsing it.

post.summary: Lookup customer details in Partner Center.
post.description:
Searches Microsoft Partner Center for matching customer
accounts by company name plus country, returning managed,
unmanaged, and Microsoft-account matches. Use this to populate
`customerProfile.ids` and `customerProfile.address` on a
subsequent `createIPReferral` call. The full Partner Center
lookup payload is accepted so callers can forward the same
body the Partner Center UI would, but only `companyName` and
`address.country` materially affect matching; other fields
are ignored.

schema.description:
Customer lookup payload. The full Partner Center customer
lookup shape is accepted, but only `companyName` and
`address.country` materially affect matching in Partner
Center -- the other address fields and the entire
`contact` block are accepted for compatibility with the
Microsoft Partner Center UI payload but are ignored by
the matching service.

addressLine1.description: Street address where the company is located.

city.description: City where the company is located.

state.description: State where the company is located.

country.description: Two digit country code where the company is located. Required, and the only address field that affects Partner Center matching.

contact.description:
Customer contact block accepted by Partner Center.
All fields are optional and ignored by the matching
service; included so callers can forward the same
payload shape that the Partner Center UI sends.

200.description: Response containing the results of the customer lookup

isvStatus.description:
Top-level lifecycle stage of the matched referral on
the ISV (partner) side. Combine with `isvSubStatus`
for the precise state. Values:

  - `None` — no status has been set yet.
  - `New` — the referral has been created and is
    awaiting action by the ISV.
  - `Active` — the referral has been accepted and
    is currently being worked on the ISV side.
  - `Closed` — the referral has reached a terminal
    state on the ISV side; see `isvSubStatus`
    (`Won`, `Lost`, `Declined`, `Expired`, `Error`)
    for the outcome.

isvSubStatus.description:
Sub-state of the matched referral on the ISV side,
scoped to the parent `isvStatus`. Values:

  - `None` — no sub-state has been set.
  - `Pending` — submission is in flight or awaiting
    acceptance.
  - `Received` — the referral has been received
    and is awaiting partner action.
  - `Accepted` — the receiving organization has
    accepted the referral.
  - `Won` — the referral closed as a won deal.
  - `Lost` — the referral closed as lost.
  - `Declined` — the receiving organization
    declined the referral.
  - `Expired` — the referral closed because no
    action was taken within Microsoft's allowed
    window.
  - `Error` — the referral closed in an error
    state.

microsoftStatus.description:
Top-level lifecycle stage of the matched referral on
the Microsoft side. Combine with `microsoftSubStatus`
for the precise state. Values:

  - `None` — no status has been set yet.
  - `New` — the referral has been created and is
    awaiting action.
  - `Active` — the referral has been accepted and
    is currently being worked on the Microsoft
    side.
  - `Closed` — the referral has reached a terminal
    state on the Microsoft side; see
    `microsoftSubStatus` for the outcome.

microsoftSubStatus.description:
Sub-state of the matched referral on the Microsoft
side, scoped to the parent `microsoftStatus`. Values:

  - `None` — no sub-state has been set.
  - `Pending` — submission to Microsoft is in
    flight or awaiting acceptance.
  - `Received` — Microsoft has received the
    referral.
  - `Accepted` — Microsoft has accepted the
    referral.
  - `Won` — the referral closed as a won deal.
  - `Lost` — the referral closed as lost.
  - `Declined` — Microsoft declined the referral.
  - `Expired` — the referral closed because no
    action was taken within Microsoft's allowed
    window.
  - `Error` — the referral closed in an error
    state.

isvAcceptedDateTime.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the ISV accepted the matched referral.

isvClosedDateTime.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the ISV closed the matched referral.

microsoftAcceptedDateTime.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when Microsoft accepted the matched referral.

microsoftClosedDateTime.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when Microsoft closed the matched referral.

post.summary: Lookup partner details in Partner Center.
post.description:
Searches Microsoft Partner Center for partner organizations
matching the supplied search text. Use the returned
`organizationId` when adding a non-Microsoft partner to a
referral via `inviteContexts`. Returns an empty `partners`
array when no matches are found.

searchText.description: Search text used to lookup the partner

200.description: Response containing the results of the partner lookup

count.description: The number of matching partners in the response

post.description:
Create a co-sell IP referral and submit it to Microsoft
Partner Center. The shape of the request and the side effect
depend on the optional `tackle-operation-id` header (default
`createIPReferral`); see the header description for the full
list of sub-operations and when to use each. Returns
`202 Accepted` immediately with a Tackle referral ID and a
`requestId` you can correlate to subsequent events via
`listReferralEvents`.

schema.description:
The unique identifier for the operation to perform when creating the referral. The header is optional; when omitted, it defaults to `createIPReferral`.

- `createIPReferral` (default): Create a new outbound IP co-sell referral and submit it to Microsoft Partner Center.
- `createDraftIPReferral`: Save a draft referral in Tackle without submitting it to Microsoft. The draft can later be submitted via `POST /api/referrals/{referral_id}` with `tackle-operation-id: createIPReferralFromDraft`.
- `cloneIPReferral`: Create a new referral by cloning an existing one. The request body must include `trackingInfo.clonedFromOpportunityId` referencing the source referral.
- `createInboundIPReferral`: **Test-environment-only.** Simulate Microsoft sharing an inbound IP co-sell referral with the ISV without making any real Partner Center calls, so customers can exercise the inbound-referral receive flow end-to-end in a test environment. Production vendors should not use this value; in production environments the request is accepted but no referral is created.

testEnvironmentInbound.summary: Test-environment-only — simulate an inbound referral from Microsoft
testEnvironmentInbound.description:
Use with `tackle-operation-id: createInboundIPReferral`. This is supported
only for vendors provisioned for use in a test environment so customers can
exercise the inbound-referral receive flow without real Microsoft Partner
Center traffic. The first entry in `inviteContexts` represents the inviting
organization (e.g. Microsoft); additional entries become related referrals on
the engagement.

value.name: Test Environment Inbound IP Co-Sell Referral

details.notes: Test environment inbound referral for receive-flow testing.

inviteContexts.notes: Microsoft is sharing this inbound referral with the ISV in a test environment.

tackleId.description: The unique identifier for the opportunity

requestId.description: Identifier for the call submitted to Microsoft Partner Center on the caller's behalf. Use it to correlate this response with subsequent referral events.

get.description:
Returns the current state of a co-sell referral by Tackle
referral ID, including both the Microsoft Partner Center
payload (`Referral`) and Tackle-side metadata
(`ReferralMetadata` -- CRM linkage, sync health, archived
state, related referrals). Returns `404 Not Found` when the
referral does not exist for the authenticated vendor.

getReferral.description: You can retrieve the referral information by providing the unique identifier for the referral.

post.description:
Update a referral. The behavior of the request depends on the
`tackle-operation-id` header. Sub-operations that look up the
referral by ID -- in particular `requestSyncFromSalesforce` --
may return `404 Not Found` when the referral does not exist for
the authenticated vendor.

schema.description:
Identifier for the sub-operation to perform when updating
the referral. Required. The value selects the request body
schema and the side-effect -- see the request-body examples
for a payload per value.

  - `updateIPReferral` -- update fields on an active outbound IP referral. Body: `UpdateReferralInput`.
  - `updateDraftIPReferral` -- update fields on a draft referral that has not been submitted to Microsoft. Body: `CreateReferralInput`.
  - `createIPReferralFromDraft` -- submit a previously-saved draft to Microsoft Partner Center. Body: `CreateReferralInput`.
  - `retryCreateIPReferral` -- retry a failed create. Body: `CreateReferralInput`.
  - `closeWonReferral` -- mark the referral closed-won. Body: `{}`.
  - `closeLostReferral` -- mark the referral closed-lost. Body: `StatusChangedInput` with `statusReason`.
  - `closeErrorReferral` -- mark the referral closed-error. Body: `StatusChangedInput` with `statusReason`.
  - `acceptIncomingReferral` -- accept an inbound referral shared by Microsoft. Body: `StatusChangedInput`; supply `team` if the referral has none.
  - `declineIncomingReferral` -- decline an inbound referral. Body: `StatusChangedInput` with `statusReason`.
  - `updateReferralCRMID` -- update the CRM linkage only; does not call Microsoft. Body: `StatusChangedInput` with `crmId` / `crmOrgId`.
  - `resyncReferralToCRM` -- re-push the latest referral state to your CRM. Body: `{}`. Does not call Microsoft.
  - `requestSyncFromSalesforce` -- pull the latest state from Salesforce. Body: `{}`. Does not call Microsoft. Returns `404` when the referral is not found for the authenticated vendor.

closeLostReferral.summary: Close a referral as lost. Should only include status reason.  Uses the StatusChangedInput schema.

closeWonReferral.summary: Close a referral as won. Should be an empty object.

closeErrorReferral.summary: Close a referral as error. Should only include status reason.  Uses the StatusChangedInput schema.

declineIncomingReferral.summary: Decline an incoming referral. Should only include status reason.  Uses the StatusChangedInput schema.

acceptIncomingReferral.summary: Accept an incoming referral. May include crmID, crmOrgID, or team.  Team must be included if the referral has no team members. Uses the StatusChangedInput schema.

retryCreateIPReferral.summary: Retry creating a referral. Uses the CreateReferralInput schema; supply the same body shape as createIPReferral. See the createIPReferral request examples for a complete payload.

updateDraftIPReferral.summary: Update a draft referral. Uses the CreateReferralInput schema; supply the same body shape as createIPReferral. See the createIPReferral request examples for a complete payload.

value.name: Test Tackle V3 Private Referral (updated draft)

updateReferralCRMID.summary: Update the CRM ID of a referral. Should only include crmId and crmOrgId.

requestSyncFromSalesforce.summary: Request a sync from Salesforce for the referral. Request body can be empty.

updateIPReferral.summary: Update a referral.  Uses the UpdateReferralInput schema.

tackleId.description: The unique identifier for the opportunity

requestId.description:
Identifier for the call submitted to Microsoft Partner Center
on the caller's behalf. Always present in the response body.
The value is the empty string for sub-operations that do not
issue a Partner Center call -- specifically
`updateReferralCRMID`, `resyncReferralToCRM`, and
`requestSyncFromSalesforce`.

get.description:
Returns the recorded history of a referral as a paginated list
of events: client-initiated operations (matching the
`tackle-operation-id` values), Microsoft Partner Center
responses, and CRM-sync history items. Use this to follow up
on a `requestId` returned from `createIPReferral` /
`updateIPReferral`, audit lifecycle changes, or surface
recent activity to end users. Pagination uses an opaque
`next` cursor.

parameters.name: next
parameters.description: Pagination cursor returned by a previous call as the `next` field. Omit on the first call.

next.description: Pagination cursor for the next page of events. Pass this value back as the `next` query parameter to fetch the next page. Omitted when there are no more results.

bearerAuth.description: Tackle machine-to-machine access token sent as `Authorization: Bearer <access_token>`.

referral_id.name: referral_id
referral_id.description: The unique identifier for the referral

BadRequest.description:
The request was malformed or could not be processed. Returned when the JSON body
cannot be parsed, when a required field is missing, when an unsupported
`tackle-operation-id` is supplied, or when a referenced CRM ID is invalid.

example.message: Your request could not be processed.

Unauthorized.description:
The request did not include a valid Tackle MTM access token, so no principal
could be established. The response body is `{}` — the `message` field is omitted.

Forbidden.description:
The authenticated principal does not have permission to perform this operation.
The response body is `{}` — the `message` field is omitted.

NotFound.description:
The requested resource was not found.

The response body shape depends on the operation:

- Read operations (for example `getReferral`) return an empty body
  (no JSON envelope).
- Write operations that look up a resource by ID before acting on it
  (for example `updateIPReferral` with `tackle-operation-id:
  requestSyncFromSalesforce`) return a JSON envelope of the form
  `{"message": "Referral not found"}`.

Conflict.description:
The request conflicts with an existing resource. For example, attempting to
create or accept a referral with a CRM ID that is already linked to another
co-sell opportunity.

example.message: A co-sell opportunity already exists for this CRM ID

InternalServerError.description:
An unexpected error occurred while processing the request. The response body is
empty.

Error.description:
Standard error envelope returned by this API. The `message` field is included
for most 4xx responses raised by request validation. For 401, 403, and 500
responses (and for `GET /api/referrals/{referral_id}` 404 responses) the body is
either `{}` or omitted entirely.

message.description: Human-readable description of the error condition.
message.example: Your request could not be processed.

ReferralMetadata.description:
Tackle-side metadata layered onto a referral when returned by
`getReferral`. Includes Tackle's stable identifier, CRM linkage
state, and sync health signals.

tackleId.description: Tackle's stable identifier for the referral. Use this as your primary key when storing co-sell records on your side.

companyName.description: Customer company name as captured by Tackle. Mirrored from the originating create payload.

companyWebsite.description: Customer company website as captured by Tackle. Not forwarded to Microsoft Partner Center.

createdDate.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the referral record was created in Tackle.

lastModifiedDate.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the referral record was last modified in Tackle.

pendingRequestIds.description: Identifiers of in-flight requests for this referral. Each entry corresponds to a `requestId` that has been issued but not yet observed in `listReferralEvents`.

crmId.description:
Identifier of the parent CRM record this referral is linked to
(typically a Salesforce 18-character Opportunity ID). 15-character
Salesforce IDs are accepted and normalized to 18 characters.

crmOrgId.description: Organization (tenant) ID of the CRM system. Required in multi-org CRM setups to disambiguate which org the `crmId` belongs to.

hasCloudErrors.description: True when at least one recent call to Microsoft Partner Center for this referral returned an error. Inspect `listReferralEvents` for details.

hasSalesforceErrors.description: True when at least one recent Salesforce sync attempt for this referral failed. Inspect `salesforceSyncError` and `listReferralEvents` for details.

salesforceSyncError.description: Most recent Salesforce sync error message recorded for this referral. Omitted when no error has been recorded.

archivedAt.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the referral was archived. Omitted when the referral is not archived.

relatedReferrals.description: Other referrals related to this one (for example, the partner-side counterpart on a partner-led co-sell engagement). Each entry is a full `Referral`.

classification.description:
Microsoft Partner Center referral classification. Values:

  - `profileMarketplaceLead` — marketplace lead from a profile listing.
  - `offerMarketplaceLead` — marketplace lead from an offer listing.
  - `coMarketingQualifiedLead` — co-marketing-qualified lead.
  - `jointPlanningQualifiedLead` — lead generated through joint planning.
  - `qualifiedLead` — generic qualified lead.
  - `solutionAssessment` — solution-assessment engagement.
  - `oemiot` — OEM IoT engagement.
  - `services` — services co-sell engagement.
  - `ip` — IP co-sell engagement.
  - `unknown` — Microsoft did not classify the referral.

dealType.description: Deal type is only applicable to referrals classified as ip or services. Newly-created referrals start as `draft` and transition to one of the other values once submitted.

lastCRMSyncCloud.description: Timestamp of the last CRM-to-Microsoft-Partner-Center sync attempt

lastCRMSyncCloudStatus.description: Status of the last CRM-to-Microsoft-Partner-Center sync attempt

lastCRMSyncCloudSuccessful.description: Timestamp of the last successful CRM-to-Microsoft-Partner-Center sync

lastCRMSyncReceived.description: Timestamp of the last data-change event received from the CRM for this referral. Updated on every data-change event (including events that result in no push to Microsoft Partner Center), so it ticks forward whenever Salesforce sends a change — independent of Microsoft Partner Center push health reported by lastCRMSyncCloudStatus.

lastCRMSyncReceivedStatus.description:
Snapshot of the referral's lifecycle state at the moment of the
last data-change event from Salesforce. This is a state label,
not a success/failure indicator — for the "did Salesforce sync
recently?" signal use `lastCRMSyncReceived`, and for sync health
use `lastCRMSyncCloudStatus`.

The set of values is open and may grow over time, so clients
should treat unrecognized values as a safe default. Current
values include (non-exhaustive): `pendingCreation`,
`pendingAcceptance`, `active`, `transitionClosedWon`,
`transitionClosedLost`, `transitionClosedError`, `closedWon`,
`closedLost`, `closedError`, `closedDeclined`.

lastCRMSyncReceivedChanges.description: Map of field name to new value applied by the last data-change event. Empty or absent when the event resulted in no field changes. Intended for future "what changed?" UI; not rendered in the current UI.

companyWebsite.description: URL of the customer organization. Captured by Tackle for context and not forwarded to Microsoft Partner Center.

crmId.description:
Identifier of the parent CRM record this referral is linked to
(typically a Salesforce 18-character Opportunity ID). 15-character
Salesforce IDs are accepted and normalized to 18 characters.

crmOrgId.description: Organization (tenant) ID of the CRM system. Required in multi-org CRM setups to disambiguate which org the `crmId` belongs to.

mpnId.description: The MPN ID of the partner

dealSensitivity.description: The sensitivity of the deal based on the selected customer.

team.description: Represents users in the organizations that are involved in the partner engagement.

inviteContexts.description: Include to invite Microsoft or another organization to the deal.

salesStage.description:
Microsoft Partner Center sales-stage code, transmitted as a
string. Microsoft's published stages map to:

  - `10` -- Accepted
  - `20` -- Qualified
  - `40` -- Developed
  - `60` -- Proposed
  - `80` -- Negotiated
  - `100` -- Won

Microsoft-defined stage codes outside this list are accepted
and forwarded unchanged, so treat the value as free-form on
the client.

team.description: Represents users in the organizations that are involved in the partner engagement. Can be used when updating or accepting a referral.

inviteContexts.description: Include to invite Microsoft or another organization to the deal.

statusReason.description: The reason the referral was declined, closed lost, or closed error.  Should be formatted as $reasonCode:$statusChangeNotes.

crmId.description:
Identifier of the parent CRM record this referral is linked to
(typically a Salesforce 18-character Opportunity ID).
15-character Salesforce IDs are accepted and normalized to 18
characters. Can be used when updating or accepting a referral.

crmOrgId.description: Organization (tenant) ID of the CRM system. Required in multi-org CRM setups to disambiguate which org the `crmId` belongs to. Can be used when updating or accepting a referral.

team.description: Represents users in the organizations that are involved in the partner engagement. Can be used when updating or accepting a referral.

operation.description:
Identifier of the action that produced this history event. The set of values is
open-ended: it includes both client-callable operation IDs (the same values
accepted by the `tackle-operation-id` request header) and additional values
recorded automatically when a CRM sync event is captured (for example,
`referral_INSERT`, `referral_MODIFY`, where the suffix reflects whether the
event recorded a new CRM record or an update). Treat this field as a free-form
string and use a default branch when displaying it.

Common values clients will see include:
  - Referral lifecycle: `createIPReferral`, `retryCreateIPReferral`,
    `createIPReferralFromDraft`, `cloneIPReferral`, `createDraftIPReferral`,
    `updateIPReferral`, `updateDraftIPReferral`, `closeWonReferral`,
    `closeLostReferral`, `closeErrorReferral`, `acceptIncomingReferral`,
    `declineIncomingReferral`.
  - CRM sync (Salesforce): `updateReferralCRMID`, `resyncReferralToCRM`,
    `requestSyncFromSalesforce`, `referral_INSERT`, `referral_MODIFY`.
  - System-generated history events: `create`, `cloudUpdateEvent`,
    `internalUpdateEvent`, `salesforceSyncRequestedEvent`.
  - Test-environment-only: `createInboundIPReferral` (emitted when a test-environment
    vendor simulates an inbound referral from Microsoft).

rawRequest.description:
Raw JSON body of the API request that produced this event,
when available. Properties depend on the originating
operation; the schema is intentionally open.

cloudRaw.description:
Full Microsoft Partner Center referral document associated with
the event, when captured (for example, on a `cloudUpdateEvent`).
Schema mirrors `Referral` but is left open because Microsoft is
the system of record for this payload.

cloudResponses.description:
Microsoft Partner Center responses recorded for this event. On
success, `rawResponse` carries Microsoft's response body. On
failure, `errorType` is set, `errorDetails` carries the
Microsoft error envelope, `errorMessage` carries a generic
message for unknown errors, and `errors` carries field-keyed
validation messages.

rawResponse.description: Raw cloud response body. Shape depends on the operation; intentionally open.

errorDetails.description:
Microsoft error envelope captured from the upstream call.
Always present in the response. On successful operations
this object is serialized with zero-value strings:
`{code: "", message: "", target: ""}`. Use `success`
and/or `errorType` to determine whether the envelope
contains a real error.

errorMessage.description: Generic error message for unknown / non-structured errors.

errors.description: Map of field name to error messages. The synthetic key `$errors` carries non-field-scoped messages.

request.description: Raw cloud request body. Shape depends on the operation; intentionally open.

crmRequests.description: CRM-side request records. Emitted for events sourced from CRM-sync history items.

requestID.description: Note that the CRM request/response records use `requestID` (capital `ID`) rather than `requestId`.

crmResponses.description: CRM-side response records. Emitted for events sourced from CRM-sync history items.

requestID.description: Note that the CRM request/response records use `requestID` (capital `ID`) rather than `requestId`.

rawResponse.description: Raw CRM response body. Shape depends on the operation; intentionally open.

errorDetails.description: Salesforce error envelope captured from the upstream call.

errorMessage.description: Generic error message for unknown / non-structured errors.

activityDetails.description:
Combined display text and event principal recorded for the
history event. The principal fields (`id`, `type`,
`givenName`, `familyName`, `pictureUrl`, `email`) describe
the principal that produced the event and are flattened
onto the same object alongside `displayText`.

id.description: Identifier of the principal that produced the event. Common values include `tackle-internal-update` (used when an update originated from an automated Tackle process) and `microsoft-update` (used when an update originated from Microsoft).

type.description:
Type of principal that produced the event. The set of values is
open; common values include:

  - `user` — an interactive Microsoft Partner Center user
    (typically authenticated with a work account).
  - `otkuser` — a Microsoft Partner Center "OTK" (one-time-key)
    user, used for service-to-service or guest principals that
    sign in without a long-lived directory account. Treat the
    same as `user` for display purposes unless your integration
    cares about the auth path.
  - `machine` — a service principal acting on behalf of an
    application rather than a person.
  - `tackle-automation` — events produced by automated Tackle
    processes (CRM sync, scheduled actions) rather than direct
    user action.

Treat unrecognized values as a safe default on the client.

organizationId.description: The organization ID of the partner.

Referral.description:
Read-side representation of a co-sell referral as returned by
`getReferral` and `listReferralEvents`. Fields are populated
from Microsoft Partner Center; `null` or omitted fields
indicate Microsoft did not return a value for that referral.

id.description: Microsoft Partner Center referral ID. Stable across the lifetime of the referral.

engagementId.description: Microsoft Partner Center engagement ID. All related referrals (for example, partner-led co-sell pairings) share the same `engagementId`.

name.description: Caller-supplied human-readable name for the referral.

externalReferenceId.description: Optional external reference ID supplied by the partner system, when present.

createdDateTime.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the referral was created.

updatedDateTime.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the referral was last updated.

expirationDateTime.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the referral will expire.

acceptedDateTime.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the referral was accepted by the receiving partner. For outgoing referrals this matches `createdDateTime`.

status.description:
Top-level lifecycle stage of the referral. Combine with
`substatus` to determine the precise state. Values:

  - `None` — no status has been set yet (typically observed only
    on draft referrals before submission to Microsoft).
  - `New` — the referral has been created and is awaiting action
    by the receiving organization.
  - `Active` — the referral has been accepted and is currently
    being worked.
  - `Closed` — the referral has reached a terminal state; see
    `substatus` (`Won`, `Lost`, `Declined`, `Expired`, `Error`)
    for the outcome.

substatus.description:
Sub-state of the referral, scoped to the parent `status`. Values:

  - `None` — no sub-state has been set.
  - `Pending` — submission to Microsoft is in flight or awaiting
    acceptance.
  - `Received` — Microsoft has received the referral and it is
    awaiting partner action.
  - `Accepted` — the receiving organization has accepted the
    referral.
  - `Won` — the referral closed as a won deal.
  - `Lost` — the referral closed as lost.
  - `Declined` — the receiving organization declined the
    referral.
  - `Expired` — the referral was closed because no action was
    taken within Microsoft's allowed window.
  - `Error` — the referral closed in an error state; see
    `statusReason` for the reported reason.

statusReason.description: Reason supplied when the referral closed (won, lost, declined, or error). Format follows `<reasonCode>:<freeFormNotes>`.

type.description:
Whether the referral is shared between the seller and a
partner organization or independent.

  - `Shared` — both sides see the referral.
  - `Independent` — only the originating organization sees it.

tags.description: Microsoft-applied tags on the referral, such as `IPCosell`. Treat as opaque labels.

qualification.description:
Sales qualification level reported by Microsoft.

  - `None` — not qualified.
  - `Direct` — direct customer interest, no MQL/SQL qualification.
  - `MarketingQualified` — marketing-qualified lead.
  - `SalesQualified` — sales-qualified lead.

team.description: Members of the partner or seller organization participating in the engagement.

eTag.description: Concurrency token for the referral as reported by Microsoft Partner Center. Treat the value as opaque.

target.description: Microsoft Partner Center targets attached to the referral (for example, the published business profile location or solution profile this referral is aimed at).

mpnId.description: Microsoft Partner Network (MPN) ID of the originating partner.

organizationId.description: Microsoft Partner Center organization ID of the originating partner.

organizationName.description: Display name of the originating partner organization.

lastModifiedVia.description: Identifier of the principal that produced the most recent modification (for example, the Microsoft Partner Center user ID or the ID of an automated process).

lastRunId.description: Identifier of the most recent processing run that touched the referral. Useful for correlating with audit logs.

referralSource.description: Source channel that produced the referral (for example, a marketplace listing or a partner-initiated co-sell).

favorite.description: Whether the referral has been marked as a favorite by the originating user.

campaignId.description: Marketing campaign ID, when the referral was created from a campaign.

salesStage.description: Microsoft Partner Center sales-stage code, transmitted as a string. See `UpdateReferralInput.salesStage` for the published code-to-stage mapping.

quality.description: Microsoft-reported lead-quality grade for the referral (for example, `Unknown`). Treat unrecognized values as a safe default.

isSpam.description: Whether Microsoft has flagged the referral as spam.

direction.description:
Whether the referral is moving outbound from the partner to
Microsoft, or inbound from Microsoft to the partner.

  - `Incoming` — the referral was originated outside the
    partner organization (for example, by Microsoft) and is
    being shared with the partner.
  - `Outgoing` — the referral was originated by the partner
    and submitted to Microsoft.

referralProgram.description: Microsoft co-sell program associated with this referral, when assigned by Microsoft.

dealSensitivity.description: Special-handling marker for the referral. Currently the only emitted value is `USFed` (US Federal customer); otherwise the value is `None`.

createdVia.description: Identifier of the principal that originally created the referral (Microsoft Partner Center user ID or automated-process ID).

closedDateTime.description: ISO-8601 timestamp recording when the referral was closed (won, lost, declined, or in error).

callToAction.description: Microsoft-suggested next action for the referral, when provided.

registrationStatus.description: Microsoft Partner Center deal-registration state for the referral (for example, `None` when registration is not applicable). Treat unrecognized values as a safe default.

isAutoRegistrationEnabled.description: Whether Microsoft will automatically register the deal on behalf of the partner.

links.description: Microsoft Partner Center HATEOAS links for follow-up navigation, keyed by relation name. See `Link`.

exception.description: Free-form exception payload captured when the referral entered an error state, when present. The value may be a structured object or a JSON-encoded string; treat as best-effort diagnostic context.

isMatchingComplete.description: If the customer was matched using the customer lookup endpoint.

isMaccEligible.description: Whether the customer is eligible for a Microsoft Azure Consumption Commitment (MACC). Copy this from the `msp_customermacceligibility` field on the matched account in the `customerLookup` response.

ids.description:
Customer organization identifiers, copied from whichever lookup
you used to find the customer:

  - From `customerLookup` -- populate `id` with
    `customerAccountDetails.msp_accountnumber` and
    `profileType: External`.
  - From a DUNS lookup -- populate `id` with the customer's
    DUNS number and `profileType: duns`.

id.description: Customer organization identifier. Source value depends on `profileType`.

profileType.description:
Identifier source. Allowed values:

  - `External` -- `id` is `customerAccountDetails.msp_accountnumber` from `customerLookup`.
  - `duns` -- `id` is the customer's DUNS number from a DUNS lookup.

team.description: The contacts for the customer organization.

AddressInput.description: Customer address used when creating a referral.

addressLine1.description:
Street address (line 1). When the customer was matched via
`customerLookup`, copy `customerAccountDetails.address1_line1`;
for DUNS-matched customers, copy `address.addressLine1` from
the DUNS lookup.

city.description:
City. When the customer was matched via `customerLookup`,
copy `customerAccountDetails.address1_city`; for DUNS-matched
customers, copy `address.city` from the DUNS lookup.

postalCode.description:
Postal code. Required only when sourced from a DUNS lookup
(use `address.postalCode` from that response); ignored when
sourced from `customerLookup`.

country.description:
Country in ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 form (see
[ISO 3166-1 alpha-2](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-2)).
When the customer was matched via `customerLookup`, convert
`customerAccountDetails.address1_country` (e.g. "United
States") to its 2-letter code (`US`); for DUNS-matched
customers, copy `address.country` from the DUNS lookup.

region.description:
Region. Required only when sourced from a DUNS lookup (use
`address.region` from that response); ignored when sourced
from `customerLookup`.

ConsentInput.description: Consent flags around sharing information with other organizations and allowing them to contact users. Required.

consentToShareReferralWithMicrosoftSelle.description: Indicates consent to share the deal with Microsoft sellers.  Note that to make a referral Partner-led, consentToShareReferralWithMicrosoftSellers is supplied as true. An active Private referral can be converted to Partner-led just by updating the referral for this field.

consentToToShareInfoWithOthers.description: Indicates consent to share personal data with others. Must be true.

consentToContact.description: Indicates consent to contact users.  Must be true.

consentToMicrosoftToContactSpecificPartn.description: Indicates consent to let Microsoft contact specific partners for this deal.

ConsentUpdateInput.description: Consent flags around sharing information with other organizations and allowing them to contact users. Required.

consentToShareReferralWithMicrosoftSelle.description: Indicates consent to share the deal with Microsoft sellers.  Note that to make a referral Partner-led, consentToShareReferralWithMicrosoftSellers is supplied as true. An active Private referral can be converted to Partner-led just by updating the referral for this field.

DetailsInput.description: Customer details, notes, deal value, currency closing date. Required.

closingDateTime.description: Date the customer is looking to close by.

RequirementsInput.description: Industry, products, service type, and solutions the customer is interested in.

solutionArea.description: The Solution area of the Customer need in the opportunity. Required for Services co-sell referrals only

solutionPlay.description: The Solution play of the Customer need in the opportunity. Required for Services co-sell referrals only

customerMarketplaceIntent.description: Indicates the customers purchase intent on Microsoft marketplace.

solutions.description: The solutions the customer is interested in.

DetailsUpdateInput.description: Customer details, notes, deal value, currency closing date. Required.

closingDateTime.description: Date the customer is looking to close by.

RequirementsUpdateInput.description: Industry, products, service type, and solutions the customer is interested in.

customerMarketplaceIntent.description: Indicates the customers purchase intent on Microsoft marketplace.

solutions.description: The solutions the customer is interested in.

type.description: The type of solution. The only currently emitted value for IP is "Name".

id.description: Identifier for the solution. For Microsoft first-party solutions, use `identifiers.id` from the Microsoft solutions response (`type: solution`); for owned or third-party solutions, use `solutionId` from the solution lookup.

name.description: Name of the solution. Use `name` from the solution lookup.

price.description: Price of the solution. Caller-supplied for Microsoft first-party (`1P`) solutions; ignored otherwise.

quantity.description: Quantity of the solution. Caller-supplied for Microsoft first-party (`1P`) solutions; ignored otherwise.

currency.description: ISO 4217 currency code. Caller-supplied for Microsoft first-party (`1P`) solutions; ignored otherwise.

solutionType.description: The type of solution.  Possible types are 1P, 3P, and SA. type from solution lookup.

publisherName.description: The solution publishers organization name.  publisherName from solution lookup.

InviteContextInput.description:
Information supplied when inviting another organization into a
co-sell engagement. Each entry in `inviteContexts` invites one
organization (Microsoft or a partner). Use the literal
`organizationId: "msft"` to invite Microsoft; use values returned
by `partnerLookup` to invite other partners.

organizationId.description: The ID of the organization being invited to participate.  “msft” for Microsoft, organizationId from partner lookup for other partners.

organizationName.description: The name of the organization being invited to participate.  “Microsoft” for Microsoft, name from partner lookup for other partners.

notes.description: Notes shared with the receiving organization. Optional, may be AI-generated for Microsoft invitees and is typically user-entered for partner invitees.

assistanceRequestCode.description:
Category describing the kind of assistance requested from the
invited organization. Used by Microsoft to route the engagement
to the right team. Allowed values:

  - `GeneralOrOther` — request that does not fit a more specific
    category.
  - `CustomerTechnicalArchitecture` — help designing the
    customer's technical architecture.
  - `ProofOfConceptOrDemo` — assistance running a proof of
    concept or product demo.
  - `QuotesOrLicensing` — assistance with pricing, quoting, or
    licensing.
  - `PostSalesCustomerSuccess` — post-sale customer-success
    engagement.
  - `WorkloadSpecificValueProposition` — help building or
    articulating a workload-specific value proposition.
  - `NoHelpNeededFromMicrosoft` — partner-led referral where no
    Microsoft assistance is requested; included so partners can
    signal intent explicitly.

dealValue.description: Deal value of the partner-side engagement. Required when inviting a non-Microsoft partner; ignored when inviting Microsoft.

currency.description:
ISO 4217 currency code (see
[Microsoft .NET ISO currency reference](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/system.globalization.regioninfo.isocurrencysymbol?view=netframework-4.7.2&preserve-view=true)).
Required when inviting a non-Microsoft partner; ignored when
inviting Microsoft.

closingDateTime.description: Date the partner is targeting for close. Required when inviting a non-Microsoft partner; ignored when inviting Microsoft.

solutions.description: Solutions the customer is interested in for this partner. Required when inviting a non-Microsoft partner; ignored when inviting Microsoft.

team.description: Members of the partner organization involved in the engagement. Required when inviting a non-Microsoft partner; ignored when inviting Microsoft.

InviteContext.description:
Read-side representation of the invite context returned on a
referral. The shape differs from the request-side
`InviteContextInput`: the inviting organization is wrapped under
`invitedBy`, and `assistanceRequestCode` is typed as a free-form
string so that any value Microsoft returns is preserved verbatim
(including values outside the input enum, such as `Unknown`).
When constructing a request, use `InviteContextInput`; when
reading a referral, expect this shape.

notes.description: Notes the inviting organization provided when inviting another organization into the partner engagement.

invitedBy.description: The organization that initiated the invite.

organizationId.description: The organization ID that sent the referral.

organizationName.description: The organization name that sent the referral.

assistanceRequestCode.description: Type of help requested by the inviting organization. Whatever value Microsoft sent is returned as-is, which can include values outside the input enum (for example `Unknown`).

invitedMpnId.description: MPN ID of the invited partner, when present.

MemberInput.description: Person on the customer or partner side participating in the engagement (a salesperson, technical contact, or executive sponsor).

phoneNumber.description: The contact's phone number, in any locale-appropriate format.

Target.description: Sales target attached to the referral, identifying which solution profile or business profile location the referral is aimed at.

id.description: Microsoft Partner Center identifier for the target resource.

type.description:
What kind of target the `id` refers to.

  - `BusinessProfileLocation` -- a published business profile location.
  - `SolutionProfile` -- a published solution profile.

Link.description: HATEOAS-style link surfaced by Microsoft Partner Center for follow-up navigation. Useful when integrating the Microsoft Partner Center UI side-by-side with a Tackle-driven flow; not required to operate this API.

uri.description: The URI of the related resource.

method.description: The HTTP method to use when following the link.

TrackingInfo.description:
Microsoft Partner Center tracking identifiers attached to the
referral. Most fields are populated by Microsoft and reflect
upstream tracking state; expect any field to be omitted when
Microsoft has not assigned a value.

microsoftMsxId.description: Microsoft Sales Experience (MSX) identifier for the linked Dynamics 365 opportunity, when present.

microsoftUSFedOpportunityId.description: Microsoft US Federal opportunity identifier, populated only for US-Federal referrals (`dealSensitivity: USFed`).

microsoftUSFedLeadId.description: Microsoft US Federal lead identifier, populated only for US-Federal referrals (`dealSensitivity: USFed`).

migratedPSCDealId.description: Legacy Partner Sales Connect (PSC) deal ID preserved on referrals migrated from PSC.

migratedPSCPartnerDealId.description: Legacy Partner Sales Connect (PSC) partner-deal ID preserved on referrals migrated from PSC.

leadToOpportunityLinkId.description: Microsoft Partner Center linkage ID joining a lead-stage referral to its converted opportunity.

microsoftMilestoneIds.description: Microsoft-side milestone identifiers associated with the referral lifecycle. Treat as opaque values.
